## 2025-08-09 - Accessibility in Data Visualization and Modern Model Evaluation
**Learning:** General-purpose or auto-generated plots (like default pandas histograms or accuracy curves) lack intuitive titles, labeled axes with unit context, and legends by default, posing accessibility hurdles. For colorblind users, raw line plots without distinguishable markers and linestyle indicators are difficult to interpret. Additionally, deprecated model prediction patterns (like `model.predict_classes()`) should be modernized to standard evaluation and decoded back to human-readable target labels for maximum clarity.
**Action:** Always enrich notebook visualization cells with explicit titles, labeled axes with units (e.g. sequence lengths and counts), and accessible markers/linestyles ('o' marker with '-' line for training, 'x' marker with '--' line for validation) along with clear legends. Modernize evaluation code to use standard prediction methods (`model.predict()`, `np.argmax()`) and map back to labels using `inverse_transform` of LabelEncoder. Clear all cell outputs and execution counts afterwards to ensure the repository remains pristine and consistent.
